newsitem.title: MEXICO: Ex-Mexico leader's brother wins a legal battle.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Mexico leader's brother wins a legal battle.

text.p: The jailed brother of former President Carlos Salinas won another legal victory on Wednesday in his bid to defend himself from a host of criminal charges that include murder and corruption.

A Mexican judge granted Raul Salinas provisional bail on charges of money laundering, although he will remain in prison on charges he plotted to murder a leading politician in 1994 and illegally amassed a fortune of more than $100 million.
He has yet to be convicted of any crime.
Mexican district judge Ricardo Ojedo Bohorquez issued the ruling a week after officials said they had started a fresh court case against him. Salinas was charged with money laundering on July 9.

Mexican officials said Salinas illegally tried to hide $13.7 million in various bank accounts held under different names. But the judge said Salinas could not be tried for money laundering until he was convicted of illegally piling up the money in the first place.

"The activity of the alleged guilty party has not been plainly proven, because it is based on other allegedly illegal activities that are still under consideration in other courts," state-owned news agency Notimex quoted the judge as saying.

The Mexican Attorney General's office issued a statement late on Wednesday said it disagreed with the judge's ruling, and added that there was sufficient reason to believe Raul Salinas' gains were ill-gotten.
"For its part, the federal Attorney General's office also believes the origin of the fortune of Raul Salinas is illegal...," the government said.
It argued that there were legal prcedents for proceeding with the case, and that it would appeal the decison.
Salinas lawyer Raul Cardenas told Reuters he was pressing the judge to drop the case altogether, saying Salinas was being tried twice for the same crime.
"A person cannot launder his own money," Cardenas said.
Salinas was cleared of tax fraud charges by a judge last year, his first victory in the long legal battles.
Authorities are continuing a separate investigation into allegations Salinas laundered or received drug money but no formal drug charges have been filed so far.
